conflict_definition: A conflict is operationalized prospectively as simultaneous findings with comparable detector severity but opposing contextual cues: signed maintenance-like lineage versus missing signer and parent-process context. These cues do not prove authorization, benignity, maliciousness, or compromise.

scenarios.description: Thirty-one inert events produce all four rule types. BEH-001, BEH-002 and BEH-003 include signed maintenance-like context, whereas BEH-004 lacks signer and parent-process context; the model must rank all findings without converting either cue into a security conclusion.
